name: SuperHQ

hlido_opinion.headline: A genuinely good idea — coding agents isolated in microVMs with diff approval — shipped as an unnotarized macOS-only binary with early-stage traction.
hlido_opinion.body: SuperHQ runs AI coding agents in real sandboxes: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and Pi, each in its own microVM, with a dashboard showing what each is working on and a review-and-merge step before changes land. The architectural argument is correct and increasingly the consensus one — giving an autonomous coding agent unmediated access to a real repository is the thing that goes wrong, and per-agent isolation with an approval gate is the right default. The remote-control story is a nice second act: pair a phone by QR, and workspaces, diffs, agent output and command execution travel with you without an app-store install. Licensing is AGPL-3.0 and the source is public. Where this loses ground is delivery. The requirements are macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon, which excludes every Linux and Windows developer and every CI environment. The page states directly that the app is not yet notarized and that macOS Gatekeeper will block it on first launch, with a documented one-time unblock step — honest disclosure, and a real barrier for exactly the security-conscious audience a sandboxing tool should attract. Traction is 180 GitHub stars and four testimonials sourced from social posts, one of which is itself a feature request asking for tool-call and network-egress logging per run. That request is the fair critique: a sandbox whose value proposition is containment currently does not surface an audit trail of what escaped it.

tier_rationale: FADING (63) not because the product is weak in conception but because the public surface shows an early-stage delivery: single-platform (macOS 14+, Apple Silicon only), an unnotarized binary that the OS blocks on first launch, 180 stars, and social-post testimonials in place of deployment evidence. Well above FLATLINE — the source is public under AGPL-3.0, the disclosure about notarization is honest, and the isolation model is sound. It moves up when the binary is signed, the platform coverage broadens, or per-run audit logging lands.
what_it_does_well: Per-agent microVM isolation is the right architectural default for autonomous coding agents
Diff review and approval before changes land, rather than trusting the agent's output
Supports three named agents out of the box (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Pi)
Remote control from any phone by QR pairing, with no app install
Discloses the Gatekeeper problem and the unblock step openly rather than hiding it
what_it_fails_at: macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon only — excludes Linux, Windows, and every CI environment
Binary is not notarized; macOS blocks it on first launch and requires a manual unblock
No per-run audit log of tool calls or network egress — the gap a testimonial itself flags
180 GitHub stars; no production deployment evidence on the surface
Testimonials are social-media quotes, not case studies or named deployments
No pricing or commercial terms visible beyond the free download
best_for: Solo developers and small teams on Apple Silicon running multiple coding agents in parallel
Anyone who wants agent changes gated behind an explicit diff approval
Developers who want to check on long-running agents from a phone
not_recommended_for: Linux or Windows developers — there is no build
Security teams that cannot accept an unnotarized binary
Organisations needing an auditable record of what an agent did inside the sandbox
red_flags: Distributed as an unnotarized macOS binary requiring a manual Gatekeeper bypass — disclosed by the vendor, but an unusual ask from a tool whose premise is security isolation

compared_to.verdict_diff: Cursor is the agent-bearing editor itself; SuperHQ is the containment layer you would run agents inside. Different jobs — but Cursor is cross-platform and commercially supported, which SuperHQ is not yet.

Aider is a mature cross-platform CLI coding agent operating directly on your repo; SuperHQ sandboxes agents like it. Aider for portability and track record, SuperHQ if isolation matters more than platform reach.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: SuperHQ is a host for agents rather than an agent-callable component: it runs Claude Code, Codex and Pi inside microVMs. Installation is a Homebrew cask, so provisioning is scriptable, but no API, MCP server or webhook surface is published for driving SuperHQ itself programmatically.
